clue.text: Start to toss a firm pancake

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of toss
taken as written
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: start by flipping a firm pancake in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss' and 'pancake' together suggest Shrove Tuesday cooking, but toss only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a folded Mexican corn tortilla, which is a flat griddle-cooked bread loosely called a pancake.

clue.text: As 24 might have been, put another way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a painting given a new frame, as the work of the artist at 24 across could be
second meaning: expressed differently, recast in other words

explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is PICASSO, here a painting by him; a canvas can be put in a new frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture fitted into a fresh frame has been reframed; an idea restated in different terms has also been reframed.

clue.text: Over 14, 16A again? It's important, after wife leaves

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so the wife's letter departs from the word

parts.note: something important is weighty
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A puzzling arithmetic aside followed by a remark about something mattering once a wife has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is SIXTY and 16 across is SCORE (twenty), so sixty plus another score makes eighty. WEIGHTY loses its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty with a further twenty added on top totals eighty, so the cross-referenced sum names the number.

clue.text: Two sentences for flyers, collectively

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime, time
life is a prison sentence for the rest of one's days

explanation.surface: A grammar exercise: compose two sentences describing flying things as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentences' suggests grammar, but both are prison terms: doing bird is British slang for serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdlife means all the birds of an area taken together, the feathered fliers considered as one group.

clue.text: Fifty times Scotsman's hugged African

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: a person who is hugged is wrapped inside someone's arms, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Ian is the typical Scottish man's name in crosswords
as in three by four, meaning multiplied

explanation.surface: Fifty times over, a Scot has embraced someone from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Libyan is a person from Libya, a country on the north coast of the continent.

clue.text: Saw head off? Flipping heck, that's archaic!

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the letters run backwards
taking the head off removes the first letter of the word in question

parts.note: a saw is an old proverb or adage

explanation.surface: Someone loses the head of a saw and swears in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool, given 'head off', but it is the old saying. 'Flipping' doubles as a mild oath in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is a dated mild oath of surprise, an old-fashioned equivalent of exclaiming heck.

clue.text: Female taking John around Great Lake

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the word for john is read back to front

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is lav
Lake Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A woman takes a man called John on a trip round one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: John reads as a man's name, but it is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerie is a girl's given name, so it stands for a woman in the crossword's usual way.

clue.text: Seafaring pirates having sex with men

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
kings are pieces, or men, in chess

explanation.surface: Raunchy tale of pirates bedding men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is the Latin word for six, so it gives the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were Norse raiders who sailed from Scandinavia plundering coastal settlements across Europe.

clue.text: Quartet that's after 12D 16As for an ageing Beatles number?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of a certain size

definitions.text: that's after 12D 16As for an ageing Beatles number?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word following threescore (sixty) in the title of a Beatles song about growing old

explanation.walkthrough: 12 down and 16 across together are THREESCORE, sixty; the Beatles sang When I'm Sixty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartet is a set of musicians numbering this many, and the same number completes the Beatles title.

clue.text: Hardy novel about a crazed nymph

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reworked name goes round the other piece
novel means new, so the author's name is made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the novelist's surname, taken as written
taken as written
crazed means mad

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy novel about a nymph driven out of her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy novel' looks like a book by Thomas Hardy, but novel is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a hamadryad is a wood nymph whose life is bound up with a particular tree.

clue.text: Tomb of old woman, lined with gold only

indicators.note: a garment lined with something has it on the inside, so those pieces go within

parts.note: one's old woman is slang for mother, mum
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: The grave of an elderly woman, its interior lined solely with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand building housing a tomb or tombs, a monumental burial place.

clue.text: Setter's after a prostitute? That's private!

indicators.note: after says the setter's word follows the other piece, so it is placed second

parts.note: tom is British slang for a prostitute
the setter speaking of what is theirs says my

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter chasing a prostitute insists the matter is confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective meaning confidential, but it is the army rank: Tommy is the traditional name for a British soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the nickname for an ordinary British soldier, a private.

clue.text: Chester outing takes round about 14

indicators.note: an outing takes the city's name out of its usual order and rearranges it

parts.note: the English city, taken as written
O is round in shape
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A day out in Chester takes in a round trip of about sixty miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is SIXTY. Chester is a cathedral city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make the number sixty in old-fashioned counting.

clue.text: One might support DUP forging alliance with one's Tory leader

parts.note: a union is an alliance
one is I, so one's becomes I'S

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the party word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Tory

explanation.surface: Northern Irish politics: a DUP backer forges a pact with the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, which propped up a Tory government in 2017.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the Democratic Unionist Party favours keeping Northern Ireland in the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Number from Rome using Los Angeles airport after vacation

definitions.text: Number from Rome using Los Angeles airport after vacation

parts.words: Number from Rome using Los Angeles airport after vacation
parts.note: surface reading: a flight number from Rome routed through LAX once the holidays end

parts.words: Number from Rome using Los Angeles airport after vacation
parts.note: setter's reading: the Roman numeral formed by emptying out the middle of the Los Angeles airport code

explanation.surface: A traveller's flight from Rome lands at LAX after the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Los Angeles airport is LAX; vacating it removes its middle letter to leave LX, the Roman numeral for this number.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman numerals L is fifty and X is ten, so LX stands for the number described.

clue.text: Some crossword, initially given free

indicators.note: initially points to the start of a word, its first letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of given
to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: A crossword handed out free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid is the pattern of black and white squares forming part of every crossword puzzle.

clue.text: See 12
Main morphine derivative in the hippocampus

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
horse is slang for heroin, which is made from morphine

explanation.surface: A neuroscience note: a chief morphine by-product acting in the brain's hippocampus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hippocampus' suggests the brain region, but it is also the zoological genus name of this fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocampus is the scientific genus containing the small upright fish with a horse-like head.

clue.text: Cunning switching of axes

indicators.note: switching swaps two things round, so the two letters of the small word change places

parts.note: taken as written
graph axes are the x and y axes

explanation.surface: A sly trick: swapping the axes on a graph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching of axes' looks like swapping x and y, but it is the little word of that switches round.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxy describes someone crafty and sly, like the fox of folklore known for its wiles.

clue.text: Duke seducing Young British Artist in Chicago?

indicators.note: seducing someone means taking them in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, as in put up your dukes
Tracey Emin was one of the Young British Artists of the 1990s

explanation.surface: A nobleman seduces a young British artist in the Windy City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicago' looks like the city but is Judy Chicago, the American artist famous for The Dinner Party; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Judy Chicago is a prominent American artist of the women's movement, so she is one example of such a campaigner.

clue.text: Make even lower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: remove the creases from, smooth flat

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'make even lower' as one phrase and it means reduce further; split it, and the first meaning comes from taking the creases out.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something is to lessen it; whimsically, ironing out creases would de-crease cloth and smooth it.

clue.text: Once more represent retiring prison officer

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: a warder is a prison guard

explanation.surface: Speak up again on behalf of a jail guard who is retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something a second time, as in a picture or map, is to draw it again.

clue.text: Mannequin's exposed hand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a model figure used to display clothes
second meaning: in bridge, declarer's partner's cards laid face up on the table

explanation.surface: A shop-window model with its hand on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's figure is called this, and in the card game bridge it names the cards laid open on the table.

clue.text: Scottish king has horse at half pace

parts.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse

indicators.note: at half means only half of the word is used, here its front portion

parts.note: a canter is a horse's pace; its front half is kept

explanation.surface: A Scottish monarch rides a horse at a half-speed gait.
explanation.walkthrough: Duncan was the Scottish king murdered in Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan I ruled Scotland in the eleventh century before Macbeth killed him and took the throne.

clue.text: Bond villain, servant who occasionally does house repairs

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun, one who does such work

parts.note: Oddjob is Goldfinger's hat-throwing henchman in the James Bond story
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A list: a Bond baddie and a servant who now and then fixes things round the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman hired now and then for small domestic repairs and maintenance tasks is known by this term.

clue.text: Out of bounds sex? Short notice, one just passed on it

definitions.text: Short notice, one just passed on it

parts.note: OB is the golfing abbreviation for out of bounds
it is a coy word for sex, or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Forbidden sex, then a brief notice about someone who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short notice' is literal: the word is short for obituary, a notice about a person who has just died.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit is the clipped form of obituary, a published notice recording someone's death.

clue.text: Number of old centre forwards missing 12D 16As from scoring position?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shirt number traditionally worn by a football centre forward
second meaning: a sexual position named after a number, with threescore (sixty) taken away

explanation.walkthrough: 12 down and 16 across together are THREESCORE, sixty; take sixty from sixty-nine, a position for scoring in the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Football centre forwards traditionally wore the shirt with this number, and sixty-nine less sixty leaves it.

clue.text: Labourer's only one against Kind of Blue

indicators.note: keeping only one of a doubled letter means its twin is dropped

parts.note: a navvy is a manual labourer
v is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A workman owns only one copy of the Miles Davis album Kind of Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Kind of Blue is a famous Miles Davis jazz album, but here it just means a shade of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy is a dark shade of blue, so it is one variety of that colour.

clue.text: Painting or photo with great appeal, on reflection

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so these letters run the other way

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, great
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Choosing between a painting and a striking photo, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: A Picasso is a work by Pablo Picasso, hence a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Picasso is an artwork by the Spanish painter Pablo Picasso, so one of his canvases is a painting.

clue.text: Not reacting, seeing 9 wearing old hat

indicators.note: something being worn sits inside the outer garment, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: old hat means passé, out of date
9 across is FOUR, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone shows no response on seeing a number wearing an old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like headgear for the container, but it is an idiom for outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: Passive describes someone accepting what happens without responding or resisting.
